ideas.title: The friends pull my first cart up the dune, feet planted in the sand
ideas.critique: This is round 1's strongest idea again, now with a mechanism for the feet: contact points inside a Coulomb cone, a gait planner that only steps where the centre of mass can follow, and a lean that comes from the tension angle. That answers the danger of a pulling animation that slides along the ground. Choosing who pulls and which rims gives the player a plan that ends in a small win at the crest. The risk is that the gait planner, the rope looped round bodies, Wong-Reece wheels and rut writing are four systems at once, and if one is faked (a canned belly-drag, a fitted mu) the whole thing becomes a rig built for one dune.

ideas.title: First ride: the cart runs away down the dune with three friends in it
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is the big goal's shared moment, with loose riders that bounce and spill by Newton, and every run can come out differently. That is something worth clipping. But it needs the cart the first idea builds, and as pitched the friends are rigid lumps with restitution, so the grab at the side is most likely added on top. A rigid friend that just tumbles will read as a ragdoll falling, not as a character.

ideas.title: Push-start: the motor stalls on the dune and the friends shove
ideas.critique: Static against kinetic resistance beating stall torque is a real reason for a push-start, and the motor and friends working together is new. But it needs the motor that barely turned to drive a cart, plus the contact model from the pull, so it cannot come first. The player's timing choice of when to touch the wire is thin, and at stall it risks being the same motor humming and barely moving.

ideas.title: The cart runs downhill and charges its own cells
ideas.critique: Braking as a resource you trade against spilling your friends is a good game choice, and the generator half of the motor is on the road. But it stacks on a cart, cells and a working motor, none of which exist yet. The glowing gauge and bubbling brine are decoration on top of a cart that rolls down a little slower, and that is hard to see on film.

ideas.title: Lumi winds the coil by hand on a lathe it turns with its foot
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Lumi's own body doing a hand skill, with the turns laid by contact and fed straight into the field solve, is a real link between how well you wind and how well the motor runs. But winding a coil is fiddly to play, and on film it is a close fixed view of a bench again. The treadle and beak guiding the wire will most likely be animated over a rod that is fed in by code.
